docs/architecture/item/decision-d3-cost-rarity-rebase.md (R1-R7; material_band map, enhance_cap rebase, curve.band-linear rebase, salvage/reroll id rebase)
docs/architecture/item/ssot-enhancement.md §7.5, §7.6 (per-level cost formulas, the shipped success-chance table)
docs/architecture/item/ssot-reroll.md §5.1 (escalation/anchor formulas — see openFindings, not curve-shaped)
_meta.conventionNote: Every point's multiplierPerMille is read as `resolvedValue = baseQty * multiplierPerMille / 1000`, the same application formula bands.v1.json's costBand already uses (baseQty defaults to 1 unless a curve's own note says otherwise). Two point styles occur below: (a) VALUE curves, where the source quantity is a game-unit/count/ms magnitude and multiplierPerMille = exactValue * 1000, so a consumer with baseQty=1 recovers the exact source number; (b) RATIO curves, where the source quantity is already a per-mille figure (a chance, an Increased ratio) and multiplierPerMille is that figure unchanged. Each entry's `notes` states which style it uses and cites its source.
_meta.idVsNameKeyNote: naming.v1.json's idNamespaces.curves gives curves the meaningless tracking template `curve.{seq:03}` with 'no translation layer needed downstream' — meaning the authored `id` becomes the literal shipped curve_id, unlike five other kinds that carry a separate runtimeId. Several source documents (ssot-materials-crafting.md §7.5, this document's own §5 example, and entry-shapes.md's drop-table example at §9) reference curves by a DESCRIPTIVE string (`curve.band-linear`, `curve.qty-material-standard`) that predates naming.v1.json's numeric template and is NOT the literal id any curve below carries. Each entry's `nameKey` preserves that descriptive string so a reviewer or a future partition can still find the right numeric id by name; a partition that writes `qtyCurve: "curve.qty-material-standard"` expecting that literal string to resolve as an id will fail import (ReferenceUnresolved) until it is corrected to the real numeric id shown here. This is flagged, not silently worked around.
openFindings: Reroll cost escalation (ESCALATION‰ = min(4000, 1000 + 250 * priorOps), ssot-reroll.md §5.1) is a closed-form formula over priorOps count, which is not one of the curve kind's three legal inputs (level/rarity/tier) and is not itself an actor/item level, rarity rung, or atom tier. No curve is authored for it: per seed-contract.md §1 ('anything a formula can compute is not authored'), a formula the reroll service already computes directly needs no lookup table, and forcing priorOps to masquerade as one of the three legal axes would be the same category error bands.v1.json warns against for dropBand vs. the rarity ladder. Likewise ANCHOR_MULT = 2^K (K = drawnCount - T) is not level/rarity/tier-keyed and is not curve-shaped for the same reason.

Drop weight by band (bands.v1.json's own dropBand.weightTable) is deliberately NOT re-expressed as a curve here. decision-d3-cost-rarity-rebase.md §Q1.6 explicitly rejects adding CurveInput.Band as a fourth curve input ('ten authored points already express [more], and it would express less'), and dropBand's weight table has no rarity/tier/level axis to key a curve on — it is a frozen, band-keyed table that already lives entirely in bands.v1.json. ssot-generation.md's own R1-R7 rarity-draw-weight table (§4.2, lines 401-409) is additionally marked illustrative-only there and is one of the four conflicting rarity vocabularies decision-d3 Q1.1 found and did not resolve into a real ten-rung weight ladder — inventing one here would be balance authorship with no source at all, not a curve derivation, so it is left undone rather than guessed.

Enhancement's essence line (essence.{element} = ceil(ilvl * L / 40), decision-d3 §Q1.4(c)) is two-axis (item level AND enhancement level) and cannot be expressed as a single level-keyed curve without inventing a reference ilvl that has no source. No curve is authored for it; the formula stays a formula, per the same seed-contract.md §1 principle.

entries.name: Band Linear
entries.notes: RATIO curve. Re-authors ssot-materials-crafting.md §7.5's `curve.band-linear` ([[1,1000],[2,2000],[3,3000],[4,4000]]) at the real ten-rung ordinal domain per decision-d3-cost-rarity-rebase.md R7 ('re-authored as ten points at x = 10, 20, ... 100. No new curve input is minted'). R7 fixes the domain but not the y-values; this file supplies them, invented with the original endpoints preserved as anchors: value(10)=1000 and value(100)=4000 match the shipped example's floor and ceiling exactly, linearly interpolated across the eight intermediate rungs (step = 3000/9, rounded to the nearest integer per-mille) so that, per R7's own rationale, two rungs inside one material band price differently instead of both clamping to 4000. Used by `material_recipe_cost.qty_curve_id`.

entries.name: Rarity Banding
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue = multiplierPerMille/1000 IS the `material_band` integer (1 common, 2 rare, 3 epic, 4 legendary). Directly reproduces decision-d3-cost-rarity-rebase.md §Q1.3's band map (itself sourced from ssot-rarity.md:298-303, R3: 'material_band ... populated from I1's own DemonRarity -> ordinal band map'). This column does not exist in core.v1.json yet (a genuine registry gap, same one entry-shapes.md §3 flags for `materials.v1.json`) — this curve is the interim authoritative source until that column lands. Also reused directly by I7's reroll costs, which need `b` (material_band) as a linear multiplier on `catalyst.flux` qty for Reforge (b) and Imprint (2b) — no separate curve needed for those; a consumer reads this curve and multiplies.

entries.name: Rarity Ceiling
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue = multiplierPerMille/1000 is the enhancement-level cap for that rung (`rarity_budget.enhance_cap`). Exact table from decision-d3-cost-rarity-rebase.md §Q1.4(b), itself constrained by ssot-rarity.md's own rule that total enhancement gain at cap stay <= one rung step in expectation. The doc marks it 'illustrative, not balanced' and notes ordinals 90 and 100 deliberately share cap 20 so almanac (the count-band ceiling) does not also get a higher enhancement ceiling stacked on top.

entries.name: Salvage Substrate
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue is `substrateBase[band]` from ssot-materials-crafting.md §5.1's `salvage_coefficient` table (band 1=2, 2=4, 3=6, 4=9), expanded from the 4-band table onto the 10-rung ordinal ladder via curve.002's rarity->band map. `SalvagePolicy.Yield` adds `+ affixes` (drawn-atom count, I8's number, not authored here) on top of this base.

entries.name: Salvage Essence
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue is `essenceCap[band]` from ssot-materials-crafting.md §5.1's `salvage_coefficient` table (band 1=0, 2=2, 3=3, 4=3). A common-band item's salvage returns zero essence regardless of elemental affix count; this is by design, not an omission.

entries.name: Salvage Shard
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue is `shardBack[band]` (of band-1) from ssot-materials-crafting.md §5.1's `salvage_coefficient` table (band 1=0, 2=1, 3=2, 4=3). R1 (§5.2): salvage always returns a shard of the band BELOW the item's own — a common item (band 1) yields no shard at all, matching the zeros here.

entries.name: Enhance Linear
entries.notes: RATIO curve (identity: value(L)/value(1) = L). Shared shape for two lines in decision-d3-cost-rarity-rebase.md §Q1.4(c)'s rebased enhancement cost, both linear in the target level L with no ceiling/floor nonlinearity: souls = 50*L (baseQty=50) and catalyst.temper = ceil(L/3) (baseQty=1/3, generator applies ceil after scaling — see ssot-materials-crafting.md §7.4's `ceil((n+1)/3)` temper rate, restated in I6's variable). Verified against decision-d3's worked table: souls at L=4/8/12/16/20 = 200/400/600/800/1000, matching `50*L` exactly.

entries.name: Shard Power
entries.notes: RATIO curve: value(L) = L^1.6 (base=1 at L=1), backing decision-d3-cost-rarity-rebase.md §Q1.4(c)'s `shard.{band} = ceil(L^1.6 / 2)` line (I6's own authoring guideline, ssot-enhancement.md §7.5). Consumer computes `ceil((1 * multiplierPerMille/1000) / 2)`. Verified against the decision doc's worked checkpoints at ilvl 64: L=4 -> ceil(9.190/2)=5, L=8 -> ceil(27.858/2)=14, L=12 -> ceil(53.295/2)=27, L=16 -> ceil(84.449/2)=43, L=20 -> ceil(120.684/2)=61 — all five match ssot-enhancement.md §7.5's published table exactly.

entries.name: Enhance Multiplier
entries.notes: RATIO curve, already the final applied multiplier (not a base-relative ratio): ssot-enhancement.md's affix scalar rule states 'each level adds +20‰ increased magnitude to the item's rolled affixes ... at +20, 1.400x'. multiplierPerMille(L) = 1000 + 20*L reproduces both endpoints exactly (L=10 -> 1200 = 1.200x, matching the doc's own +10 worked example; L=20 -> 1400 = 1.400x). Applies only to rolled affixes — implicits and milestone atoms are never scaled by this curve.

entries.name: Enhance Fortune
entries.notes: RATIO curve, already the applied figure: this IS the chance in per-mille, not a ratio against a base. Reproduces ssot-enhancement.md §7.6's shipped `item_enhance_rules` table verbatim ('Success chance before pity'): +1..+8 flat at 1000‰ (the safe band never fails), then falling to 200‰ at +20. Pity (+80‰ per failure, persisted per-instance, reset on success) is a runtime accumulator, not part of this base curve.

entries.name: Tier Magnitude
entries.notes: RATIO curve: the cumulative form of bands.v1.json's `powerBand.tierScaling.magnitudeRatioPerMille` (1750‰ per-step, r=1.75), i.e. multiplierPerMille(t) = round(1000 * 1.75^(t-1)). This is the default shape 'shared by every channel-family group' per bands.v1.json unless a family's own tier-bands input overrides it (out of this registry's scope, owned by I8's not-yet-built tier-bands artefact). A family with no worked example of its own (see curve.012-curve.016 for the five that have one) resolves its m_t as `m1 * multiplierPerMille(t)/1000`, where m1 itself comes from a `sharePermille` this file does not supply.

entries.name: Tier Duration
entries.notes: RATIO curve: the cumulative form of bands.v1.json's `powerBand.tierScaling.durationRatioPerMille` (1400‰ per-step, r=1.4), i.e. multiplierPerMille(t) = round(1000 * 1.4^(t-1)). MANDATORY for a status.apply family's duration ladder (bands.v1.json: 'control families ladder duration at r=1.4, never at 1.75' — a 1.75 ladder would put tier-5 control near 7.5s and let three items chain a permanent lock). Never applies to a magnitude or trigger-chance ladder; use curve.011 for those.

entries.name: Vitality Curve
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue = multiplierPerMille/1000 is the tier midpoint in game units (maxHp, Flat op). Reproduces bands.v1.json's `powerBand.channelFamilyGroups.primaryChannel.workedExamples[vitality]` verbatim (sharePermille=30 against BattleRuleset.BaseHp(20)=680, per ssot-affixes.md §4.5). Marked there as 'illustrative, inherited, not balanced' — reproduced here for calibration, not re-derived. The +/-33% band width around each midpoint (lo/hi) is `variance: "normal"`'s job (bands.v1.json), not this curve's.

entries.name: Might Magnitude
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue is the tier midpoint in game units (atk, Flat op). Reproduces bands.v1.json's `primaryChannel.workedExamples[might]` verbatim (sharePermille=45 against BattleRuleset.BaseAtk(20)=92). Tier-1 resolves to 4 game units, below the registry's own 5-unit legibility floor (bands.v1.json's `tierScaling.overlap.knownEdgeCase`) — the documented fix lives on `ferocity` (curve.015), never here; kept as-is deliberately.

entries.name: Ferocity Magnitude
entries.notes: RATIO curve, already the applied figure: ferocity is `Increased atk`, so its tier value IS a per-mille figure natively (no *1000 scaling — do not confuse these small numbers with the VALUE-curve convention used elsewhere in this file). Reproduces bands.v1.json's `primaryChannel.workedExamples[ferocity]` verbatim (sharePermille=16 legibilised to a tier-1 midpoint of 15‰, exactly as the source notes).

entries.name: Sigmoid Magnitude
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue is the tier midpoint in sigmoid resolver points (AccuracyScale=CritRateScale=CritDamageScale=100.0, so 100 points = one full sigmoid unit). Reproduces bands.v1.json's `sigmoidDerivedChannel.workedExamples[0]` verbatim — the exact numeric table ssot-affixes.md §4.5 authored under the (incorrect, per the units-correction ledger) name `elemental_power`, reassigned here to the placeholder sigmoid family it arithmetically belongs to. Anchored so tier 5 lands near ~50 points, a third of the 150-point critical-hunter calibration trait. No correctly-named sigmoid family (precision, keen_edge, ...) has authored its own table yet; this is the only one that exists.

entries.name: Freezing Chance
entries.notes: RATIO curve, already the applied chance in per-mille. Reproduces bands.v1.json's `statusMagnitudeAndDuration.workedExample[freezing]` chance column verbatim. Pair with curve.018 for this same family's duration ladder — the two-ladder rule (bands.v1.json) requires them to scale at different ratios (1.75 vs 1.4), which is why chance and duration are never combined into one curve.

entries.name: Freezing Duration
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue = multiplierPerMille/1000 is the tier's duration in milliseconds. Reproduces bands.v1.json's `statusMagnitudeAndDuration.workedExample[freezing]` duration column verbatim (800ms at t1 rising to 2900ms at t5, the mandatory r=1.4 duration ratio). Large multiplierPerMille values are an artifact of this file's uniform base=1/VALUE convention applied to a millisecond-scale magnitude, not an error.

entries.name: Material Yield
entries.notes: INVENTED, no source. Mints the curve id entry-shapes.md §9's drop-table example cites (`qtyCurve: "curve.qty-material-standard"`) so that reference has something to resolve to; the reference itself is illustrative, not a numbers commitment from any lane document. RATIO curve, base=1 at level 1: a stacking material's drop quantity grows modestly (1.0x -> 3.0x) with the dropping content's level. `input: level` here means the content/actor level of the drop source, not enhancement level (curve.007-010) or item level (curve.024) — see this file's `_meta.idVsNameKeyNote`/`openFindings` for the level-axis ambiguity this schema does not resolve. Will need refitting against real drop-volume data before it should be treated as balanced.

entries.name: Pool Floor
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue is `rarity.ladder[].countBand.min`, read directly from the FROZEN core.v1.json registry (not a lane document) — chaff draws 0 affixes (base type plus implicit only), almanac's floor is 5. Pairs with curve.021 for the ceiling.

entries.name: Pool Ceiling
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue is `rarity.ladder[].countBand.max`, read directly from the FROZEN core.v1.json registry. Almanac's ceiling is 6 affixes, one more than its floor of 5 — the one rung whose count band is not two-wide.

entries.name: Window Floor
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue is `rarity.ladder[].tierWindow.min`, read directly from the FROZEN core.v1.json registry. Chaff's tierWindow is `null` (no pool at all) and is encoded here as 0, a sentinel outside the real 1-5 tier domain, consistent with chaff's 0-affix count band (curve.020) making the window moot.

entries.name: Window Ceiling
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue is `rarity.ladder[].tierWindow.max`, read directly from the FROZEN core.v1.json registry. Chaff encoded as 0 (see curve.022's note). Four of the top five rungs (70-100) share ceiling t5 — the ladder differentiates those rungs by count band (curve.020/021) and window floor (curve.022), not by how high the window reaches.

entries.name: Tier Threshold
entries.notes: VALUE curve, base=1: resolvedValue is the minimum item level (ilvl) at which a given atom tier may appear, reproduced verbatim from ssot-generation.md's 'Tier | Minimum ilvl' table (t1=1, t2=1, t3=8, t4=18, t5=32). `input: tier` here is the unambiguous atom-tier axis (bands.v1.json's `powerBand.tierMap`), not the level-of-a-level ambiguity flagged on curve.019 — tier 1-5 has exactly one meaning across this whole corpus.
